units.title: A Gaussian polynomial feature has its actual ambient L² derivative
units.classification: canonical shared library node; original mathematical supplement
units.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure, let γ be its centered standard Gaussian law with identity covariance, and let p be any finite real polynomial. For every ambient w and every direction v, both f_w(x)=p(⟨w,x⟩) and d_{w,v}(x)=p′(⟨w,x⟩)⟨v,x⟩ belong to L²(γ). There exist simultaneous membership witnesses and a field D(w):E→L²(γ) of continuous real linear maps such that D(w)v is exactly the class of d_{w,v}. The actual feature-class map Φ(w)=[f_w] is fully Fréchet differentiable at every ambient w, with derivative D(w). No feature membership, derivative membership, domination, differentiability or operator bound is an input.
assumptions: E has real inner-product normed, finite-dimensional and Borel structures; no positive dimension is required.
p is any finite real polynomial, including zero, constant and non-even polynomials. The weight w ranges over all of E.

steps.title: Produce Gaussian radial domination
steps.text: Finite Gaussian norm moments and polynomial induction give L² radial envelopes on each bounded weight ball. Applying them to p and p′ times one radial factor produces the actual feature and directional-derivative memberships.
steps.formula: |p(\langle u,x\rangle)|\le B_0(x),\quad |p\prime(\langle u,x\rangle)|\,\|x\|\le B_1(x),\qquad B_0,B_1\in L^2(\gamma).
steps.lean:
private theorem polynomial_radial_envelope
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (p : Polynomial ℝ) (R : ℝ) (hR : 0 ≤ R) (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ B : E → ℝ, MemLp B 2 (stdGaussian E) ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ B x) ∧
      ∀ (w : E), ‖w‖ ≤ R → ∀ x,
        ‖p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * ‖x‖^k ≤ B x := by
  classical
  letI : CompleteSpace E := FiniteDimensional.complete ℝ E
  letI : SecondCountableTopology E := inferInstance
  let μ := stdGaussian E
  have hpow (n : ℕ) : MemLp (fun x : E => ‖x‖^n) 2 μ := by
    apply (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq (by fun_prop)).2
    have hi := (IsGaussian.memLp_id μ ((2*n : ℕ) : ℝ≥0∞)
      (ENNReal.natCast_ne_top (2*n))).integrable_norm_pow' (p := 2*n)
    convert hi using 1
    funext x
    simp only [id_eq, ← pow_mul, Nat.mul_comm n 2]
  induction p using Polynomial.induction_on' with
  | add p q hp hq =>
    obtain ⟨B,hB,hB0,hBp⟩ := hp
    obtain ⟨C,hC,hC0,hCq⟩ := hq
    refine ⟨B+C,hB.add hC,fun x => add_nonneg (hB0 x) (hC0 x),?_⟩
    intro w hw x
    calc
      ‖(p+q).eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * ‖x‖^k ≤
          (‖p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖+‖q.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖) * ‖x‖^k := by
        rw [Polynomial.eval_add]
        exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (norm_add_le _ _) (pow_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) _)
      _ = ‖p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * ‖x‖^k + ‖q.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * ‖x‖^k := by ring
      _ ≤ (B+C) x := add_le_add (hBp w hw x) (hCq w hw x)
  | monomial n a =>
    refine ⟨fun x => (‖a‖*R^n)*‖x‖^(n+k),
      (hpow (n+k)).const_mul (‖a‖*R^n),fun x => by positivity,?_⟩
    intro w hw x
    have hi : ‖⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ ≤ R*‖x‖ :=
      (norm_inner_le_norm (𝕜 := ℝ) w x).trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hw (norm_nonneg _))
    simp only [Polynomial.eval_monomial,norm_mul,norm_pow]
    calc
      ‖a‖ * ‖⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖^n * ‖x‖^k ≤ ‖a‖ * (R*‖x‖)^n * ‖x‖^k := by
        gcongr
      _ = (‖a‖*R^n)*‖x‖^(n+k) := by rw [pow_add,mul_pow];ring

private theorem ambient_feature_and_derivative_memLp
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (p : Polynomial ℝ) :
    (∀ w : E, MemLp (fun x : E => p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ) 2 (stdGaussian E)) ∧
      ∀ w v : E, MemLp (fun x : E =>
        p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ * ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ) 2 (stdGaussian E) := by
  constructor
  · intro w
    obtain ⟨B,hB,hB0,hBound⟩ :=
      polynomial_radial_envelope (E := E) p ‖w‖ (norm_nonneg _) 0
    apply hB.mono' (by fun_prop)
    exact ae_of_all _ fun x => by simpa using hBound w le_rfl x
  · intro w v
    obtain ⟨B,hB,hB0,hBound⟩ :=
      polynomial_radial_envelope (E := E) p.derivative ‖w‖ (norm_nonneg _) 1
    apply (hB.const_mul ‖v‖).mono' (by fun_prop)
    apply ae_of_all _
    intro x
    calc
      ‖p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ * ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ‖ =
          ‖p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * ‖⟪v,x⟫_ℝ‖ := norm_mul _ _
      _ ≤ ‖p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * (‖v‖*‖x‖) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (norm_inner_le_norm (𝕜 := ℝ) v x) (norm_nonneg _)
      _ = ‖v‖ * (‖p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * ‖x‖) := by ring
      _ ≤ ‖v‖ * B x := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
        (by simpa using hBound w le_rfl x) (norm_nonneg _)

steps.title: Build the represented bounded linear map
steps.text: The directional scalar formula is linear in v. Its L² norm is bounded by an envelope norm times ‖v‖, so it extends directly to a continuous linear map with the required actual-class identity.
steps.lean:
private theorem represented_derivative_clm
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (p : Polynomial ℝ)
    (hdf : ∀ w v : E, MemLp (fun x : E =>
      p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ * ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ) 2 (stdGaussian E)) :
    ∃ D : E → E →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E),
      ∀ w v, D w v = (hdf w v).toLp
        (fun x : E => p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ * ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ) := by
  classical
  have hD (w : E) : ∃ D : E →L[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E),
      ∀ v, D v = (hdf w v).toLp
        (fun x : E => p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ * ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ) := by
    let df := fun (v x : E) => p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ * ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ
    let L : E →ₗ[ℝ] Lp ℝ 2 (stdGaussian E) := {
      toFun := fun v => (hdf w v).toLp (df v)
      map_add' := by
        intro v u
        apply Lp.ext
        filter_upwards [(hdf w (v+u)).coeFn_toLp,
          Lp.coeFn_add ((hdf w v).toLp (df v)) ((hdf w u).toLp (df u)),
          (hdf w v).coeFn_toLp,(hdf w u).coeFn_toLp] with x hsum hadd hv hu
        simp only [Pi.add_apply] at hadd
        rw [hsum,hadd,hv,hu]
        simp [df,inner_add_left,mul_add]
      map_smul' := by
        intro c v
        apply Lp.ext
        filter_upwards [(hdf w (c • v)).coeFn_toLp,
          Lp.coeFn_smul c ((hdf w v).toLp (df v)),(hdf w v).coeFn_toLp] with x hcv hsmul hv
        simp only [Pi.smul_apply,smul_eq_mul] at hsmul
        simp only [RingHom.id_apply]
        rw [hcv,hsmul,hv]
        simp [df,real_inner_smul_left]
        ring }
    obtain ⟨B,hB,hB0,hBound⟩ :=
      polynomial_radial_envelope (E := E) p.derivative ‖w‖ (norm_nonneg _) 1
    let b := hB.toLp B
    have hnorm (v : E) : ‖L v‖ ≤ ‖v‖ * ‖b‖ := by
      apply Lp.norm_le_mul_norm_of_ae_le_mul
      filter_upwards [(hdf w v).coeFn_toLp,hB.coeFn_toLp] with x hv hBx
      change ‖(hdf w v).toLp (df v) x‖ ≤ ‖v‖ * ‖b x‖
      rw [hv]
      change ‖df v x‖ ≤ ‖v‖ * ‖hB.toLp B x‖
      rw [hBx,Real.norm_of_nonneg (hB0 x)]
      calc
        ‖df v x‖ = ‖p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * ‖⟪v,x⟫_ℝ‖ := norm_mul _ _
        _ ≤ ‖p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * (‖v‖*‖x‖) :=
          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (norm_inner_le_norm (𝕜 := ℝ) v x) (norm_nonneg _)
        _ = ‖v‖ * (‖p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * ‖x‖) := by ring
        _ ≤ ‖v‖ * B x := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
          (by simpa using hBound w le_rfl x) (norm_nonneg _)
    refine ⟨L.mkContinuous ‖b‖ (fun v => by simpa [mul_comm] using hnorm v),?_⟩
    intro v
    rfl
  choose D hD using hD
  exact ⟨D,hD⟩

steps.title: Differentiate the pointwise polynomial
steps.text: Polynomial differentiation composed with the inner-product functional yields the genuine scalar derivative for every x and every direction.

steps.title: Control the normalized remainder locally
steps.text: A local scalar mean-value bound and the directional bound dominate the normalized scalar remainder by twice one L² envelope. At u=w define the inverse-norm normalization by the usual totalized value zero.
steps.formula: r_u(x)=p(\langle u,x\rangle)-p(\langle w,x\rangle)-p\prime(\langle w,x\rangle)\langle u-w,x\rangle,\quad q_u(x)=\|u-w\|^{-1}|r_u(x)|\le2B(x).
steps.lean:
private theorem local_increment_bounds
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]
    (p : Polynomial ℝ) (w : E) :
    ∃ B : E → ℝ, MemLp B 2 (stdGaussian E) ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ B x) ∧
      (∀ u : E, ‖u-w‖ ≤ 1 → ∀ x,
        ‖p.eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ - p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ ≤ B x * ‖u-w‖) ∧
      ∀ (v x : E), ‖p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ * ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ‖ ≤ B x * ‖v‖ := by
  obtain ⟨B,hB,hB0,hBound⟩ := polynomial_radial_envelope
    (E := E) p.derivative (‖w‖+1) (by positivity) 1
  have hwNorm : ‖w‖ ≤ ‖w‖+1 := by linarith
  refine ⟨B,hB,hB0,?_,?_⟩
  · intro u hu x
    have huNorm : ‖u‖ ≤ ‖w‖+1 := by
      calc
        ‖u‖ = ‖(u-w)+w‖ := by rw [sub_add_cancel]
        _ ≤ ‖u-w‖+‖w‖ := norm_add_le _ _
        _ ≤ ‖w‖+1 := by linarith
    have hwMem : w ∈ Metric.closedBall (0 : E) (‖w‖+1) := by
      simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right] using hwNorm
    have huMem : u ∈ Metric.closedBall (0 : E) (‖w‖+1) := by
      simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right] using huNorm
    apply (convex_closedBall (0 : E) (‖w‖+1)).norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le
      (fun z hz => (pointwise_ridge_hasFDerivAt p z x).hasFDerivWithinAt) ?_ hwMem huMem
    intro z hz
    rw [norm_smul,innerSL_apply_norm]
    have hzNorm : ‖z‖ ≤ ‖w‖+1 := by
      simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right] using hz
    simpa only [pow_one] using hBound z hzNorm x
  · intro v x
    calc
      ‖p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ * ⟪v,x⟫_ℝ‖ =
          ‖p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * ‖⟪v,x⟫_ℝ‖ := norm_mul _ _
      _ ≤ ‖p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * (‖v‖*‖x‖) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (norm_inner_le_norm (𝕜 := ℝ) v x) (norm_nonneg _)
      _ = (‖p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ‖ * ‖x‖) * ‖v‖ := by ring
      _ ≤ B x * ‖v‖ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right
        (by simpa only [pow_one] using hBound w hwNorm x) (norm_nonneg _)

  let r := fun (u x : E) => p.eval ⟪u,x⟫_ℝ - p.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ -
    p.derivative.eval ⟪w,x⟫_ℝ * ⟪u-w,x⟫_ℝ
  let q := fun (u x : E) => ‖u-w‖⁻¹ * ‖r u x‖
  obtain ⟨B,hB,hB0,hInc,hDir⟩ := local_increment_bounds p w
  have hR (u : E) (hu : ‖u-w‖ ≤ 1) (x : E) :
      ‖r u x‖ ≤ (2 * B x) * ‖u-w‖ := by
    exact (norm_sub_le _ _).trans ((add_le_add (hInc u hu x) (hDir (u-w) x)).trans_eq (by ring))
  have hq (u : E) (hu : ‖u-w‖ ≤ 1) (x : E) : q u x ≤ 2 * B x := by
    by_cases h : u = w
    · subst u
      simpa [q] using hB0 x
    · have hn : 0 < ‖u-w‖ := norm_pos_iff.mpr (sub_ne_zero.mpr h)
      calc
        q u x ≤ ‖u-w‖⁻¹ * ((2 * B x) * ‖u-w‖) :=
          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hR u hu x) (inv_nonneg.mpr (norm_nonneg _))
        _ = 2 * B x := by field_simp
  have hq0 (x : E) : q w x = 0 := by simp [q]

steps.title: Use dominated convergence on the squared remainder
steps.text: Pointwise Fréchet differentiability gives q_u(x)→0, and 4B² is integrable. Dominated convergence therefore controls the whole L² remainder, not just each fixed directional limit.
steps.lean:
have hqcont (x : E) : ContinuousAt (fun u : E => q u x) w := by
    rw [ContinuousAt,hq0]
    have ht := (hasFDerivAt_iff_tendsto.mp (pointwise_ridge_hasFDerivAt p w x))
    simpa only [q,r,ContinuousLinearMap.smul_apply,innerSL_apply_apply,
      smul_eq_mul,real_inner_comm x] using ht
  have hBsq : Integrable (fun x => 4 * (B x)^2) μ :=
    ((memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq hB.1).1 hB).const_mul 4
  have hc : ContinuousAt (fun u : E => ∫ x, (q u x)^2 ∂μ) w := by
    apply continuousAt_of_dominated (bound := fun x => 4 * (B x)^2)
    · exact Eventually.of_forall fun u => by dsimp [q,r]; fun_prop
    · filter_upwards [Metric.closedBall_mem_nhds w (by norm_num : (0:ℝ)<1)] with u hu
      have hu' : ‖u-w‖ ≤ 1 := by simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_eq_norm] using hu

        rw [Real.norm_eq_abs,abs_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg _)]

        have h := (sq_le_sq₀ hnon (mul_nonneg (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 2) (hB0 x))).2 (hq u hu' x)

    · exact hBsq
    · exact ae_of_all _ fun x => (hqcont x).pow 2

steps.title: Identify the actual quotient norm
steps.text: Almost-everywhere identities for subtraction, scalar multiplication and toLp identify the displayed integral with the squared norm of the normalized genuine class remainder. Taking its square root proves the full ambient Fréchet limit.
steps.lean:

    rw [← real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq,L2.inner_def]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    have hd := (hdf w (u-w)).coeFn_toLp
    rw [← hD w (u-w)] at hd
    filter_upwards [Lp.coeFn_smul ‖u-w‖⁻¹ (R u),
      Lp.coeFn_sub (F u - F w) (D w (u-w)),
      Lp.coeFn_sub (F u) (F w),(hf u).coeFn_toLp,(hf w).coeFn_toLp,hd]
      with x hsm hsub hsub' hfu hfw hdx

      change (‖u-w‖⁻¹ • R u) x = _

      rw [hsub]
      simp only [Pi.sub_apply]
      rw [hsub']
      simp only [Pi.sub_apply]
      change ‖u-w‖⁻¹ * ((hf u).toLp _ x - (hf w).toLp _ x - D w (u-w) x) = _
      rw [hfu,hfw,hdx]
    rw [hval]

units.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure, let γ be its centered standard Gaussian law with identity covariance, and let p be any finite real polynomial. For every ambient weight w and direction v, the actual functions f_w(x)=p(⟨w,x⟩) and d_{w,v}(x)=p′(⟨w,x⟩)⟨v,x⟩ belong to L²(γ). steps.title: Use the actual marginals for every coupling
steps.text: Every feasible coupling is a probability. Marginal pushforward identities and Bochner subtraction express the actual mean difference as one integral of feature increments.

private theorem actual_coupling_mean_difference
    {U H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace U]
    [NormedAddCommGroup H] [NormedSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]
    (K : U → H) (hK : StronglyMeasurable K) (B : ℝ)
    (hBound : ∀ u, ‖K u‖ ≤ B)
    (μ ν : Measure U) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (γ : Measure (U × U))
    (hγ : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport.IsCoupling γ μ ν) :
    (∫ u, K u ∂μ) - (∫ v, K v ∂ν) = ∫ z, (K z.1-K z.2) ∂γ := by

    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport.isProbabilityMeasure_of_isCoupling_left hγ
  have hleft : Integrable (fun z : U × U => K z.1) γ :=
    bounded_feature_integrable _ (hK.comp_measurable measurable_fst) B
      (fun z => hBound z.1) γ
  have hright : Integrable (fun z : U × U => K z.2) γ :=
    bounded_feature_integrable _ (hK.comp_measurable measurable_snd) B
      (fun z => hBound z.2) γ
  have hfst : (∫ u, K u ∂μ) = ∫ z, K z.1 ∂γ := by
    rw [← hγ.1]
    exact integral_map_of_stronglyMeasurable measurable_fst hK
  have hsnd : (∫ v, K v ∂ν) = ∫ z, K z.2 ∂γ := by
    rw [← hγ.2]
    exact integral_map_of_stronglyMeasurable measurable_snd hK

steps.title: Square the integral bound
steps.text: The feature increment hypothesis first bounds the mean norm by L∫c dπ. Nonnegativity of ∫(c−∫c)² gives the probability square-integral inequality, without an assumed cost estimate.
steps.formula: \left(\int c\,d\pi\right)^2\le\int c^2\,d\pi,\qquad A^2\le L^2\int c^2\,d\pi,\quad A=\left\|\int K\,d\mu-\int K\,d\nu\right\|.
steps.lean:
private theorem probability_square_integral_le
    {α : Type*} [MeasurableSpace α] (γ : Measure α) [IsProbabilityMeasure γ]
    (f : α → ℝ) (hf : MemLp f 2 γ) :
    (∫ x, f x ∂γ)^2 ≤ ∫ x, (f x)^2 ∂γ := by
  let m := ∫ x, f x ∂γ
  have hi : Integrable f γ := hf.integrable (by norm_num)
  have hs : Integrable (fun x => (f x)^2) γ := (memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq hf.1).1 hf
  have hm : Integrable (fun x => 2 * f x * m) γ := (hi.const_mul 2).mul_const m
  have hn : 0 ≤ ∫ x, (f x-m)^2 ∂γ := integral_nonneg fun x => sq_nonneg _
  have he : (∫ x, (f x-m)^2 ∂γ) = (∫ x, (f x)^2 ∂γ)-m^2 := by
    simp_rw [sub_sq]
    have hsub : Integrable (fun x => (f x)^2-2*f x*m) γ := hs.sub hm
    rw [integral_add hsub (integrable_const (m^2)),integral_sub hs hm]
    simp only [integral_mul_const,integral_const_mul,integral_const,probReal_univ,one_smul]
    change (∫ x, (f x)^2 ∂γ) - 2*m*m + m^2 = _
    ring
  rw [he] at hn
  change m^2 ≤ _
  linarith

private theorem actual_coupling_squared_mean_bound
    {U H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace U]
    [NormedAddCommGroup H] [NormedSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H]
    (K : U → H) (hK : StronglyMeasurable K) (B C L : ℝ)
    (hC : 0 ≤ C) (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hBound : ∀ u, ‖K u‖ ≤ B)
    (c : U × U → ℝ) (hc : Measurable c)
    (hc0 : ∀ z, 0 ≤ c z) (hcBound : ∀ z, c z ≤ C)
    (hLip : ∀ u v, ‖K u-K v‖ ≤ L*c (u,v))
    (μ ν : Measure U) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (γ : Measure (U × U))
    (hγ : AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport.IsCoupling γ μ ν) :
    ‖(∫ u, K u ∂μ)-(∫ v, K v ∂ν)‖^2 ≤ L^2 * ∫ z, (c z)^2 ∂γ := by
  letI : IsProbabilityMeasure γ :=
    AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport.isProbabilityMeasure_of_isCoupling_left hγ
  have hcLp : MemLp c 2 γ := (memLp_const C).mono' hc.aestronglyMeasurable
    (ae_of_all _ fun z => by simpa only [Real.norm_of_nonneg (hc0 z)] using hcBound z)
  have hcInt : Integrable c γ := hcLp.integrable (by norm_num)
  have hleft : Integrable (fun z : U × U => K z.1) γ := bounded_feature_integrable _
    (hK.comp_measurable measurable_fst) B (fun z => hBound z.1) γ
  have hright : Integrable (fun z : U × U => K z.2) γ := bounded_feature_integrable _
    (hK.comp_measurable measurable_snd) B (fun z => hBound z.2) γ
  have hnorm : ‖(∫ u, K u ∂μ)-(∫ v, K v ∂ν)‖ ≤ L * ∫ z, c z ∂γ := by
    rw [actual_coupling_mean_difference K hK B hBound μ ν γ hγ]
    calc
      ‖∫ z, (K z.1-K z.2) ∂γ‖ ≤ ∫ z, ‖K z.1-K z.2‖ ∂γ := norm_integral_le_integral_norm _
      _ ≤ ∫ z, L*c z ∂γ := integral_mono (hleft.sub hright).norm
        (hcInt.const_mul L) (fun z => hLip z.1 z.2)
      _ = L * ∫ z, c z ∂γ := integral_const_mul _ _
  have hm0 : 0 ≤ ∫ z, c z ∂γ := integral_nonneg hc0
  have hs := (sq_le_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg hL hm0)).2 hnorm
  calc
    ‖(∫ u, K u ∂μ)-(∫ v, K v ∂ν)‖^2 ≤ (L * ∫ z, c z ∂γ)^2 := hs
    _ = L^2 * (∫ z, c z ∂γ)^2 := mul_pow _ _ _
    _ ≤ L^2 * ∫ z, (c z)^2 ∂γ := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left
      (probability_square_integral_le γ c hcLp) (sq_nonneg _)

units.lean_statement: Let U be any measurable space and H a complete real normed vector space. Let K:U→H be strongly measurable with ‖K(u)‖≤B. Let c:U×U→ℝ be measurable with 0≤c(z)≤C, and suppose ‖K(u)−K(v)‖≤L c(u,v), where B,C,L≥0. For any two probability measures μ,ν on U, define Q as the infimum, over all actual couplings π with these two marginals, of ∫c² dπ, interpreted as an extended nonnegative integral; set W=Q^(1/2). Then K is genuinely Bochner integrable under each law, Q is finite, and ‖∫K dμ−∫K dν‖≤L W.toReal. For every y∈H both residual norms are at most B+‖y‖. No optimizer, chosen-plan bound, finite-cost assumption or mean-identity premise is supplied. U need not carry a vector-space structure, and c need not be a metric.
